title: Ancient Egyptian Hieroglyphics
text: Hieroglyphics was the formal writing system used in ancient Egypt, combining logographic and alphabetic elements. The system consisted of over 700 distinct signs, including phonograms (representing sounds), logograms (representing words), and determinatives (indicating word categories). Hieroglyphics were used primarily for monumental inscriptions on tombs, temples, and obelisks. A cursive form called hieratic was used for administrative records. The Rosetta Stone, discovered by French soldiers in 1799 during Napoleon's Egyptian campaign, was inscribed with the same text in hieroglyphics, Demotic, and Greek. Thomas Young and Jean-François Champollion used it to decipher hieroglyphics by 1822, opening Egypt's ancient texts to modern scholarship.
